newsitem.title: USA: NYS tax collections total $19.8 bln thru October.
newsitem.headline: NYS tax collections total $19.8 bln thru October.

text.p: New York State tax collections for all governmental funds for fiscal year 1997 totaled $19.8 billion, a 4.5 percent increase over the same period last year, the state comptroller's office reported on Thursday.

"I continue to see results better than were anticipated when the budget was passed," state Comptroller H. Carl McCall said in a statement. "Following my report last month that the year would end with a surplus, the Governor revised his financial plan. The updated plan takes a cautious approach, and reserves $300 million for litigation."

Personal income tax witholding is down 2.4 percent over the same period last year because of tax cuts, but estimated payments are up 16.5 percent. Total personal income tax collections are up 5.4 percent to $102 billion.
Three quarters of the increase from last year in the personal income tax is attributtable to last year's surplus, which counts as a collection this year.
Sales tax is up 4.3 percent while total consumer taxes and fees are uo 1.7 percent to $5.4 billion. Business taxes are up 4.3 percent to $3.4 billion. Other taxes are up 15.7 percent to $731 million.
Miscellaneous receipts increased 4.7 percent to $4.8 billion. Federal funds increased 1.6 percent to $11.6 billion.
Disbursements for all governmental funds were up slightly to $35.3 billion through October, representing 1.7 percent growth.
"Although it appears that the State's budgetary position has improved, much of that improvement is attributable to the financial markets, which tend to be volatile," McCall said.
